We have $CG = |x_G - x_C| = |x_G - 26| = 40$, so $x_G - 26 = 40$ or $x_G - 26 = -40$.
Thus, $x_G = 66$ or $x_G = -14$.

$x_F = 36 + (73 - 36) = 36 + 37 = 73$.

$$ \frac{1}{2} | (x_B(y_E - y_G) + x_E(y_G - y_B) + x_G(y_B - y_E)) | $$
Since the points are collinear, we can assume the coordinates are such that $y_B = y_E = y_G = 0$. Then the area is 0.

However, we are given that $CG = 40$ and $DG = 30$.

Let $BG = |x_B - x_G| = |14 - 66| = 52$.
Let $GE = |x_E - x_G| = |57 - 66| = 9$.

$x_F = 96 + (73 - 96) = 96 - 23 = 73$.

$BG = |74 - 66| = 8$.
$GE = |57 - 66| = 9$.
$BE = |57 - 74| = 17$.
$s = \frac{8+9+17}{2} = \frac{34}{2} = 17$.
The area of $\triangle BGE = \sqrt{17(17-8)(17-9)(17-17)} = \sqrt{17(9)(8)(0)} = 0$.

In either case, the points $B, G, E$ are collinear, so the area of $\triangle BGE$ is 0.

Let $A = 0$. Then $C = 26$, $B = x_B$, $D = x_B+22$, $E = x_B+22+31 = x_B+53$, $F = x_B+53+33 = x_B+86$.
Also, $AF = 73$, so $x_B+86 = 73$, which gives $x_B = 73-86 = -13$.
Then $B = -13$, $C = 26$, $D = -13+22 = 9$, $E = 9+53 = 62$, $F = 62+33 = 95$.
